AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guards N1 and G1 per binding rule 4. Count, selection prompt and deck placement are all faithful; the named Niche RNG stream is dropped (N1, live for RNG parity) and the candidate list omits C#'s Quest-card exclusion (G1, dormant).

guards.what: N1 (LIVE for RNG parity): C# names `Rng.Niche` and the stream IS consumed; run.transform_card is called with no pick_rng, so the sim silently falls back to the legacy shared random.Random
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the port now draws on the named stream. sts2_rl/relics/new_leaf.py:20-22 resolves `niche = run.rng_set.niche` and passes `pick_rng=niche` to run.transform_card, which is CardCmd.TransformToRandom(item, RunState.Rng.Niche) (NewLeaf.cs:27) reaching CreateRandomCardForTransform; the legacy RL path keeps the shared rng by convention. WAS: the call went to the legacy shared random.Random, so the stream was never advanced and every later draw off it read at the wrong position.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForTransformation also excludes Quest cards; run.transformable_cards() filters only Eternal
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForTransformation (CardSelectCmd.cs:485-491) builds its candidate list as `Cards.Where(c => c.Type != CardType.Quest && c.IsTransformable)`. run.transformable_cards() (run.py:364-366) returns removable_cards(), i.e. every non-Eternal deck card, with no Quest clause -- its own docstring says 'in the deck this equals IsRemovable', which is true of IsTransformable (CardModel.cs:739-750) but ignores the caller's extra filter. So the sim can offer a Quest card for transformation where the game cannot. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, and the concrete blocker is named): the three ported Quest cards -- byrdonis_egg, lantern_key, spoils_map (executed census; all three have eternal=False, so nothing else excludes them) -- enter the deck only through later events (events/byrdonis_nest.py:45, events/the_lantern_key.py:44, events/the_legends_were_true.py:41), while New Leaf is granted ONLY at floor 0, by Neow or by relic/neows_bones drawing from the same pool, when the deck is still the pristine starting deck. What would make it live: any grant path for New Leaf after floor 0 (a relic-trade event that can hand out Ancient relics, or a second source). NOTE THE POOL-WIDE SHAPE, filed in .superpowers/sdd/relic-batch-10-lessons.md: run.transformable_cards() is the shared helper for relic/leafy_poultice and five ported events (events/endless_conveyor.py:97, morphic_grove.py:44, symbiote.py:52, trial.py:99, whispering_hollow.py:66), all of which ARE reachable after a Quest card can be in the deck -- so the mechanism is live somewhere, just not at this relic's site. Rule 7: CardSelectCmd.cs, CardModel.cs, run.py and every events/*.py named above are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: CardsVar(1) (NewLeaf.cs:18) read as `.IntValue` into CardSelectorPrefs (NewLeaf.cs:24) vs the literal 1 (new_leaf.py:16)
guards.rationale: NewLeaf.cs contains no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension call, so 1 is the pinned non-ascension value.

guards.what: N3: FromDeckForTransformation's auto-select shortcut -- `if (list.Count <= prefs.MinSelect && !RequireManualConfirmation) enumerable = list;` (CardSelectCmd.cs:493-496)
guards.rationale: run.select_cards (run.py:371-390) clamps `count = min(count, len(candidates))` and returns everything when the pool is at or below the requested count, which is the same behaviour: with one transformable card left, both sides transform it with no choice offered. The sim delegates the actual pick to run.card_selector when installed and otherwise samples with the run rng, which is the house model for a player choice.

guards.what: N4: deck placement of the replacement (PROMPT.md bug class 8)
guards.rationale: CardCmd.Transform on a DECK pile removes the original and APPENDS the replacement at the end of the deck (CardCmd.cs:437); run.transform_card's docstring (run.py:418-428) cites that line and implements the end-placement for the parity path, which is what keeps the combat-start shuffle in parity. Nothing relic-specific diverges here; recorded because the class was checked.

RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / UpdateDisplay / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.PreviewCardPileAdd are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text, and animation timing.
